At PetZone Mahalaxmi Veterinary Clinic, we are dedicated to the health and well-being of your beloved pets. Knowing when to seek immediate veterinary attention can make all the difference in emergency situations. Here are some critical warning signs that indicate your pet may require urgent care:

2. **Sudden Lethargy**: If your pet suddenly becomes unusually tired or inactive, it could be a sign of a serious underlying condition.

3. **Refusal to Eat for More Than 24 Hours**: A sudden loss of appetite, especially when prolonged, can indicate different health threats.

4. **Seizures**: Whether single or multiple, seizures are a medical emergency requiring prompt attention.

5. **Bloating**: Noticeable swelling in the abdomen can signal an emergency, such as gastric dilatation-volvulus in dogs.

featured_reviews.review_text:
​​I am extremely disappointed with the care provided to my cat, Pintu, at this clinic. We brought her in with the very specific and concerning symptoms that she was completely refusing to eat and constantly hiding. Despite spending 11k on diagnostics and treatment, she is still facing the exact same issues with zero improvement—she is still not eating, still hiding, and still suffering.

​To make matters worse, yesterday, at the exact moment we were leaving the clinic to take her back home, they suddenly demanded an additional 7k. They claimed she has an infection and that we would have to pay this extra amount for the "next procedure." Springing massive, unexpected financial demands at the last minute—before the initial 11k treatment has even shown a single positive result for her main symptoms—feels completely unprofessional and exploitative.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Mr. Salvi, we are surprised to see this review as you haven't visited our premises yourself and it was Ms. Padawe who brought Pintu in. We are unaware of how you are connected to this case but we would still like to clarify.

We are sorry that you feel this way and would like to bring you some relief by actually narrating what really happened at our premises. Pintu was presented with inappetence and weakness, and all diagnostics, treatment plans, and estimated costs were discussed, signed and approved before proceeding by Ms. Padawe. Throughout her diagnostic tests and treatment, we provided updates regarding her condition as she was boarded with us for medical supervision through the day.

The statement that an additional ₹7,000 was suddenly demanded before leaving is completely inaccurate. The amount was discussed and approved beforehand and was for a specific diagnostic test that was strongly suggested because we needed to arrive at a definitive diagnosis with no prior history of an indoor-outdoor cat like Pintu. 

It is also important to understand that cats suffering from infectious or systemic illnesses may not recover completely within a single day of treatment. Improvement often requires several days of consistent medication, supportive care, and follow-up monitoring.

Regarding the concern that Pintu ran away after receiving her medication, there is no medical basis to conclude that the prescribed medication caused her to leave the house, as you mentioned that she is an indoor outdoor cat already. Cats experiencing illness, stress, or discomfort may hide or become less visible, and this behavior was part of the original concerns for which she was presented, infact you mentioned  she was so weak that she couldn't move and after treatment she had enough energy to run away from home when tried to feed medication. At the time, we provided guidance and continued to assist you through messages regarding her care at home multiple times.

We also provided advice regarding medication administration and feeding, and recommended that Pintu be brought back for treatment if you don't see an improvement in her condition after she returned home. Unfortunately, the recommended follow-up treatment was not carried out by you.

We fully understand how distressing it is when a pet is unwell. However, it is important that the outcome of a medical case be assessed based on the complete course of treatment and follow-up rather than just the first 12 hours after discharge.

Our team remains committed to providing transparent communication, appropriate medical care, and support to every patient and pet owner.  

After leaving us the above review Ms. Padawe still reached out to ask for more assistance and we still happily obliged as it's Pintu's wellbeing that has always been our priority. 
We sincerely wish Pintu a full and speedy recovery and honestly hope that you follow through with the recommended diagnostics and treatment wherever you choose to take Pintu

You were informed that there were two ways to go ahead.. to do a biopsy that would confirm the lymphoma and its type or to just go ahead and treat it without the biopsy and were given estimates for both. You were given estimates for any and every consult, investigation and treatment proposed and your informed consent taken before proceeding with any of them. Since you have a completely contrasting opinion, despite the FNAC report suggestive of a lymphoma, only time will tell who was right or wrong.. we really hope that we are wrong this time and that Sniffy has a long healthy life and your decision to conserve money and not do any additional investigation was the correct one

I’m so relieved and happy that Blue 7 Vets has now opened a branch in South Mumbai! For the past 4 years I’ve been taking all my pets to their Borivali clinic, and it’s such a blessing that the same team of excellent doctors and staff are now dividing their time between the two branches. Having a full-service clinic so close to home—with in-house ultrasound, X-ray, blood tests, and even a fully equipped OT—really gives me peace of mind. It's right opposite Antilia, so it's pretty easy to locate with a few parking spots as well.

I recently visited with my cat for her vaccination and overall check-up, and as always, Dr. Vineet handled her with such care. Despite her being very scared, he performed a thorough check-up gently and patiently, and also guided us with our newly adopted indie pup. What I truly value is how his strong medical expertise is complemented by his deep understanding of animal behaviour and psychology, which makes his advice both practical for us and stress-free for the pets.

South Mumbai finally has a one-of-a-kind clinic, and I couldn’t be more grateful! Despite so many clinics being there, we finally have one which doesn't make you wait during emergencies and their treatment can be trusted!

Advice: Call in advance and take an appointment to avoid waiting too long for your turn.

I am writing this review to warn other pet parents.
This clinic was unhygienic, and my cat was not handled with proper cleanliness, care, or monitoring. Basic hygiene and attention to a sick animal were clearly lacking.
After treatment here (injections and saline), my cat’s condition rapidly deteriorated. She developed continuous loose motions, repeated vomiting, extreme weakness, and breathing difficulty — all serious emergency warning signs.

featured_reviews.name: Armaan Bhatia
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went with my cat there, she had some internal problem related to birth of a premature baby done at a young age, I take the blame on me for not taking her to the hospital on time, but whatever I've experienced there was no less comforting. I'll write the start to finish of what I've seen and experienced.

•The greeting:
At gate they ask you for ₹10, still okay as they let you go in first and look for payment later. Although when I admitted my cat, they asked for more for their "chai nashta" Which isn't necessary as she's a part of the ward.

•Ward:
I don't know about any other ward personally, but for CATS, there are 4 wards(wardA, B, C & D), my cat was in ward D, and it wasn't "comfortable for patient" type. They have cages in a room on which they lay a sheet of diaper and keep your cat with food and water. And if they don't have diapers, they'll make them lay on the cage's floor which is a welcome for the cat to catch cold. Plus there were red ants in the cage, and the hygiene wasn't up to mark, specially for cats who have cuts that can get maggots or infections in them due to such a rest place

•The Medical Ward:
They have only 4 tables/stretchers for Animals, alot less for a hospital so big.

1) The medical ward is mostly filled with ward boys, the people who have the job to LOOK AFTER PATIENTS in the WARD.

2) There are 1-2 main doctors, in which One of them was constantly sitting on his chair while the substitute/junior doctors came over to ask him for what to do. It was more looked like a biology class where students were asking the teacher for help.. WHILE ANIMALS WERE FIGHTING FOR LIFE. The second doctor was helpful, he was treating animals which I'll praise him for.

3) The ward boys, despite being more than 15 there, weren't taking the MOMENT seriously. They were actively talking, joking, hanging around as if they're in a park. And if you have a pet waiting to be treated with a table empty infront of you, the ward boy won't even look at you, he would instead go somewhere and just stand, clearly showing he Is currently free but not helping.

4) note, the medical ward is ONLY open between 10:00 - 13:00.

5) while they were injecting my cat, instead of focusing on her, they were actively talking. My cat even went under a shock where she almost died but was recovered.

6) while taking her blood for blood test, the doctor squeezed her leg(from where they took the blood) to get samples, It's understandable as she got skinny due to the lack of food and water, but after the work, they didn't massage or rubbed the part of the leg to losen the squeezed muscle down. Because of which, 10 minutes after keeping her in a basket, I noticed her leg being stained by her blood.

•Treatment of a passed away body:
When I reached hospital after hearing my cat's loss, I looked for her in the ward, medical room, etc. When I asked someone, he took me to a room where my cat's body was kept in a pull-away trolley with a dusty rug kept over her. As a animal parent, I can't see my cat's body being kept like trash, Atleast keep her on the hoodie I provided, idc if she doesn't feel the comfort anymore, but that'd atleast give me a relief that she had my presence around her until her last breath.

Note: I take responsibility for the death of my cat, im not saying that they allegedly kill them. My point is, where a human patient would usually get full care for even a small wound, the animals on other hand aren't given that much. The hygiene and prioritizing style of the hospital isn't quite much. It's almost as they don't take the animal as a living being. It's a decent hospital, but keep your beloved there at your own risk.

We are deeply saddened by the loss of your kitten, and we sincerely understand how painful and emotional such a situation can be for any pet parent. Our heartfelt condolences are with you during this difficult time.

However, we would like to respectfully clarify certain statements made in this review.

The kitten was examined and treated based on the symptoms and diagnostic findings presented during each visit. Necessary consultations, prescriptions, medications, blood tests, IV fluids, and supportive treatments were advised according to the kitten’s condition at that time. All investigations and treatments were discussed with the owners before proceeding.

Throughout the treatment period, our doctors and staff remained in constant touch with the owners. Messages and calls were responded to promptly, including late-night communication at around 12:40 AM. Whenever concerns were raised, guidance was provided immediately.

When the owners informed us that the kitten was experiencing breathing difficulty and respiratory distress, they were advised without delay to bring the kitten to the hospital immediately for emergency treatment and monitoring. Relevant call and chat records regarding these communications are available.

After the initial treatment period at our clinic, the owners also chose to continue treatment at a government hospital. Additionally, our doctors had repeatedly advised timely vaccination for the kitten as part of preventive care. However, the owners informed us on multiple occasions that they intended to get the vaccinations done elsewhere.

It is also incorrect to state that excessive fees were charged. Each visit, including consultation, treatment, medications, and tests, was billed transparently, and no individual bill exceeded approximately ₹1100. Bills and prescriptions were provided throughout the treatment period.

The kitten’s condition involved serious complications including viral infection, jaundice, vomiting, electrolyte imbalance, and later respiratory distress. Veterinary medicine, especially in very young kittens with severe systemic illness, can sometimes involve sudden deterioration despite timely medical care and supportive treatment.

We completely understand the grief and distress associated with losing a young pet. However, we strongly deny allegations of negligence or intentional carelessness by our doctors or staff. Our team made sincere efforts to guide, treat, and support the case throughout the period the kitten was under our care.

We remain committed to providing compassionate, ethical, and responsible veterinary care to every patient entrusted to us.
